**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Typical Value / Description |
|----------|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| **Physical State at STP** | Phase | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (120.2 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14 K) |
| | Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat of fusion | 0.000 kJ mol⁻¹ (negligible) |
| | Refractive index (visible) | ~1.000132 |
| | Viscosity (at 25 °C) | 8.76 × 10⁻⁶ Pa·s |
| | Surface tension | 0.002 N m⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation state | +1 (in most compounds) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy (gas) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (ΔH° ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Reactivity | Highly flammable; reacts with halogens, metals, and many oxidants under suitable conditions |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (hydrogen ion donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) |
| | Redox behavior | Can be reduced to metal (protium) or oxidized to water; participates in hydrogen bonding |
| **Spectroscopic Properties** | Rotational constant (J=1→0) | 60.853 GHz |
| | Vibrational frequency (ν₁) | 4401 cm⁻¹ (for H₂) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H₂) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Dipole moment | 0 (homonuclear diatomic) |
| | Magnetic moment (proton) | 2.7928 μ_N |
| **Isotopic Variations** | ¹H (protium) | Stable, most abundant (~99.98 %) |
| | ²H (deuterium) | Stable, ~0.02 % natural abundance |
| | ³H (tritium) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion and radiolabeling |
| **Applications & Significance** | Energy carrier | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant |
| | Industrial uses | Ammonia synthesis (Haber process), methanol production, petroleum refining |
| | Scientific research | Calibration standards, quantum chemistry tests, astrophysical observations |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (water only) but requires renewable production to be truly green |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, consisting of one proton and one electron.
- **Highly reactive**: It readily forms bonds with many elements, especially oxygen, nitrogen, and halogens.
- **Energy potential**: When used in fuel cells or combustion, it produces only water, making it a clean energy vector—provided the hydrogen itself is produced from renewable sources.
- **Isotopic diversity**: The presence of stable deuterium and radioactive tritium gives hydrogen unique roles in scientific research and nuclear technology.
- **Spectroscopic benchmark**: Its simple molecular structure makes H₂ a standard reference in spectroscopy and quantum mechanical studies.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
